stories.title: Bank of Canada governor warns of second‑round oil‑linked inflation in 2027
stories.summary: In a speech to the Economic Club of Canada in Toronto, Governor Tiff Macklem said high energy prices are expected to keep pressuring consumers at the pump and beyond in 2027, even as oil prices have fallen. He warned that larger and more frequent supply shocks could produce a second‑round effect of the recent Middle‑East oil shock, adding to inflation persistence. The remarks followed his earlier announcement that he will not seek a second term.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.

stories.previousSummary: In a speech to the Economic Club of Canada in Toronto, Governor Tiff Macklem said that despite recent declines in benchmark oil prices, high energy costs will keep pressuring consumers at the pump and beyond in 2027. stories.title: BBC analysis of leaked Rosstat data finds at least 490,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
stories.summary: The BBC examined more than 11 million death records from Russia’s statistics agency (Rosstat) covering 2021 to September 2026, obtained after hacks attributed to the Belarusian group Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine’s Silent Crow. The analysis shows that at least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the invasion began in 2022. The Kremlin says only the defence ministry can officially report casualties and has not released figures for several years.
stories.why: The estimate offers the first publicly available glimpse of Russian military fatalities, shaping understanding of the war’s human cost and informing policy and public debate.

stories.title: Amazon acquires Decart for $7.5 billion to boost Trainium AI chip performance
stories.summary: Amazon announced it will acquire Decart’s technology and team for a reported $7.5 billion. Decart’s Optimization Stack improves AI model efficiency on non‑Nvidia hardware, and Amazon plans to integrate it with its Trainium chips to increase performance and expand AWS AI services. The deal follows reported interest from Anthropic and Nvidia and builds on a collaboration that began in 2025.
stories.why: The acquisition gives Amazon a software layer to narrow the performance gap with Nvidia’s chips, enhancing its AI cloud offering.
stories.previousTitle: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
stories.previousSummary: But there was another development yesterday that could also matter for Nvidia down the road: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart‘s tech and its team for a reported $7.5 billion. Anthropic reportedly tried to acquire the startup in the same ballpark, and Nvidia, which invested in the startup’s $300 million funding round at a $4 billion valuation, was also rumored as a prospective buyer.

stories.title: Tidal to ban fully AI‑generated songs and delete millions of tracks
stories.summary: Tidal announced it will begin removing songs that are entirely generated by artificial intelligence starting December 9, with an expected deletion of more than 29 million tracks by year‑end. The service said AI‑generated uploads made up over 43 % of new uploads in the past 90 days, leading to a daily rejection of roughly 80,000–85,000 tracks. Tidal will still accept songs that use AI assistance but will block 100 % AI submissions and ban distribution services that deliver them.
stories.why: To stem the flood of fully AI‑generated uploads that are overwhelming the platform’s catalog.
stories.previousTitle: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
stories.previousSummary: Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.

stories.title: RBI steps up scrutiny of importers' forex deals after split‑transaction pattern emerges
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has increased scrutiny of foreign‑exchange transactions by importers after detecting that some companies are breaking up purchases into amounts below the $2 million threshold to avoid higher reserve requirements. Data show a sharp decline in the average size of dollar‑buying transactions since October 10, even as the total number of deals has risen, leading the RBI to launch fresh compliance checks on banks that process these trades.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.
